title: Fractions, Units and Necessary Conditions
overview: A fraction names selected equal parts of one whole. This short lesson keeps two conditions in view: compare or add fractions only when they share the same whole, and repartition a fraction only by multiplying the numerator and denominator by the same positive integer.
scopeNote: Covers fraction meaning, unit and count, same-whole checks, equivalent fractions, and same-whole addition; differing wholes are described, not treated as comparable.

lessons.title: Same Whole, Same Unit
lessons.objective: Explain why fractions must share one whole before their quantities are compared, how the denominator names the unit and the numerator counts units, how one positive integer preserves quantity, and how a common unit makes addition valid.
lessons.focus: Whole, unit, count. Compare only under the same whole. Equivalent fractions need the same positive integer on both numerator and denominator. Add through a common unit; adding denominators gives the wrong unit.
